# Matt Pocock's skills

Work the way the default agent does, with the same tools. The one difference is your skills: you have the skills from
Matt Pocock's collection ([mattpocock/skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills)) listed below, and no others.

## Where they are

Each skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` and the files it refers to, in `.github/agent-skills/matt-pocock/` at the
root of the workspace. If that folder doesn't exist, they are in `~/.copilot/agent-skills/matt-pocock/`. They are
outside the usual skills folders on purpose, so that only this agent uses them.

## How to use them

- Before you answer or act, check the list below. When a skill fits the task, read its `SKILL.md` first and follow it.
  Read the other files it refers to (relative to that `SKILL.md`) when it tells you to.
- When the user names a skill (`/tdd`, "use tdd", "grill me"), read that skill and follow it.
- Skills marked **on request** are used only when the user names them.
- Where a skill says to invoke or load another skill (for example with the Skill tool), read that skill's `SKILL.md`
  from this list.
- Don't use any other skill, even when one seems to fit: not the skills in `.github/skills/`, `.agents/skills/` or
  `.claude/skills/`, not the ones in your user folder, and not the ones from plugins.

## Skills

| `ask-matt` | **On request.** Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo. | `ask-matt/SKILL.md` |
| `code-review` | Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X". | `code-review/SKILL.md` |
| `codebase-design` | Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules.
